columns.name: SequenceNumber
columns.definition: Defines this occurrence's sequential order in the series. The sequence will be an integer from 1 to N, where N is typically no higher than 6. The absolute max value is determined by the smallint datatype.

columns.name: AbsoluteMin
columns.definition: The minimum amount of time that must elapse, relative to a reference date, before this occurrence is allowed to be completed.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: AbsoluteMax
columns.definition: The maximum amount of time that is allowed elapse, relative to a reference date, before this occurrence is no longer allowed to be completed.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: RecommendedMin
columns.definition: The recommended amount of time that should elapse, relative to a reference date, before this occurrence should be completed.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: RecommendedMax
columns.definition: The recommended amount of time that could potentially be allowed to elapse, relative to a reference date, before this occurrence should have already been completed. This max would represent the end of the date range that this occurrence is scheduled. An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: PrevOccurrenceMax
columns.definition: For the previous occurrence, this is the recommended amount of time that could potentially be allowed to elapse, relative to a reference date, before this occurrence should have already been completed. This max would represent the end of the date range that this occurrence is scheduled. An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: NextOccurrenceRecGapMin
columns.definition: The recommended minimum amount of time, relative to the scheduled or completed data of this occurrence, that should elapse before the next occurrence should be scheduled or completed.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: NextOccurrenceRecGapMax
columns.definition: The recommended maximum amount of time, relative to the scheduled or completed data of this occurrence, that should elapse before the next occurrence should be scheduled or completed.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

tables.definition: The Billed Transaction and Billed Transaction Detail tables contain the Audit History for the Billing Interface. This data represents the parameters used to generate the data in the Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail tables below.Financial TransactionBilled Audit Trail Financial Transaction consists of one Billed Transaction and 1 or more Billed Transaction Details.There is one Billed Transaction for each Bill Charge HeaderThere is one Billed Transaction Detail for each Bill Charge Detail.If there was an Error returned by Determine Price, the Billing Interface will still create a Billed Transaction and the associated Billed Transaction Detail records, but will not create corresponding Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail rows.Billed TransactionBilled Transaction identifies Patient and Order related information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the PID segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System.Billed Transaction DetailBilled Transaction Detail identifies Drug, Cost, and Price information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the FT1 segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System.Billed TransactionBilled Transaction identifies Patient and Order related information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the PID segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System.Billed Transaction DetailBilled Transaction Detail identifies Drug, Cost, and Price information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the FT1 segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System.

columns.definition: Add a column to the task to identify it as a Follow-up task called, TaskSeqNum. This Sequence number will be an integer equivalent to the sequence number from the Follow-up task�s CatalogTaskItem. Tasks that are not Follow-up tasks (i.e. Primary/external) will always have a TaskSeqNum of 0. This id will be used to determine the display order of the tasks, in combination with the tasks StartDtm (which will be the primary performed dtm + the offset time). 0 indicates this is a primary task. >0 indicates this is a followup task

columns.name: HasFollowupTask

Copy to new task when the original primary is cancelled.

columns.name: MaxAdminID
columns.definition: Maximum Administration ID used for all occurrences for this task. Set only on primary tasks (TaskSeqNum = 0).

Each CVX code for a Vaccine would be associated with a separate row and a unique name.

tables.definition: This entity defines the Price Algorithm Range Rules for a Price Algorithm.A set of range rules is optional for a Price Algorithm. If it does not not exist, then the Price (amount to bill) is equal to the cost.A range rule is tiered, so a different set of rules can be applied based upon which range (Cost From / Cost To) the Cost falls into.A range rule includes markups, fees, a rounding option, and minimum price functionality. Two sets of tiers can be applied for the same Price Algorithm - 'multi ingredient', or 'non multi ingredient'. Multi Ingredient indicates that the product being dispensed is a multi-ingredient product (made up of several ingredients), and therefore a separate tiered pricing structure should apply.

columns.name: FromCostAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the From Cost range of the Price Algorithm.If the Cost is between the From Cost Amt and the To Cost Amt, and the Is Multi Ingredient indicator matches whether the drugs are multi-ingredient, then this is the range rule (fees, markups) that are applied to the cost to determine the price.

columns.name: ToCostAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the To Cost range of the Price Algorithm.If the Cost is between the From Cost Amt and the To Cost Amt, and the Is Multi Ingredient indicator matches whether the drugs are multi-ingredient, then this is the range rule (fees, markups) that are applied to the cost to determine the price.

columns.name: IsMultiIngredient
columns.definition: Identifies whether this Tiered Price Algorithm is for Multi-Ingredient, or for Single-Ingredient.

columns.name: MarkupType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [None],1 = [Amount],2 = [Percent],

columns.name: MarkupAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Markup (based on the Markup Type).If Markup Type indicates 'Percent', then this is a percentage markup.If Markup Type indicates 'Amount', then this is a Dollar markup.,

columns.name: DispensingFeeType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [None],1 = [Amount],2 = [Percent],

columns.name: DispensingFeeAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Dispensing Fee (based on the Dispensing Fee Type).If Dispensing Fee Type indicates 'Percent', then this is a percentage Fee.If Dispensing Fee Type indicates 'Amount', then this is a Dollar Fee.

columns.name: CompoundingFeeAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Compounding Fee (if there is one) that should be applied.This is the fee applied for creating the order.Commonly used as reimbursement for effort used in dispensing multi-ingredient orders.,

columns.name: AdministrationFeeAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Administration Fee (if there is one) that should be applied.,

columns.name: RoundUpAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Round Up amount (if there is one).Round up to the nearest unit specified.The main values used are:0.01 - Round up to the nearest Cent0.10 - Round up to the nearest Dime 0.50 - Round up to the nearest half dollar1.00 - Round up to the nearest DollarAny value can be specified (for example 1.25 would indicate to round up to the nearest Dollar and 25 Cents).Default of Blank will round to the nearest Cent and is equivalent to 0.01.,

columns.name: MinimumPriceAmt
columns.definition: Identifies a Minimum price for the tiered range.If the Price determined as a result of applying the Price Algorithm is less than this Minimum Price, then this Minimum Price is the Price of the Stock Item Product ,

tables.definition: Defines the individual observation item and headings for a flowsheet configuration. When adding observations to flowsheets (can only add a observation to a master flowsheet), the entries are inserted into this table. The entries in this table are related one to one with the entries in CV3ObservationEntryItem.

columns.name: SiteID
columns.definition: Identifies the unique distributed database ID where the row was inserted. Distributed databases are no longer supported so this column is deprecated.

columns.name: RepFlags
columns.definition: Indicates the action in a distributed database environment. Distributed databases are no longer supported so this column is deprecated.

columns.name: Build
columns.definition: Identifies the build number and patch level of the software that inserted/updated this row. The format is the Build number followed by 3 digits for the patch level which is typically 000. The build number is tied to specific versions of the software, e.g. Sunrise 15.3 is Build 5021, Sunrise 16.3 is Build 5503.

columns.name: TouchedBy
columns.definition: Information about the user that last updated the row. This will typically be the UserID (IDCode from CV3User table) and may be prefixed with an environment identifier followed by an underscore, e.g. b96d2bf5_jongmore.

columns.name: TouchedWhen
columns.definition: The date and time that the row was last updated and will be based on the Enterprise time zone.

columns.name: CreatedBy
columns.definition: Information about the user that created the row. This will typically be the UserID (IDCode from CV3User table) and may be prefixed with an environment identifier followed by an underscore, e.g. b96d2bf5_jongmore.

columns.name: CreatedWhen
columns.definition: The date and time that the row was created and will be based on the Enterprise time zone.

columns.name: Active
columns.definition: Denotes whether the row is active or not, 0 means the row has been soft deleted or deactivated.

columns.name: GUID
columns.definition: Unique primary key value.

columns.name: VersionGUID
columns.definition: A foreign key to the GUID column in the CV3FlowsheetVersion table.

columns.name: IsMasterVersion
columns.definition: A flag that indicates if this item is part of the master (default) version of the flowsheet. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: ObsEntryItemGUID
columns.definition: A foreign key to the GUID column in the CV3ObservationEntryItem table.

columns.name: IsIncluded
columns.definition: A flag that indicates if this Observation Entry Item is to be included in this version of the flowsheet. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: DisplayName
columns.definition: The display name for this item as it is to appear in the flowsheet for this version.

columns.name: BackgroundColor
columns.definition: Indicates the background color for this row.

columns.name: IsColorExtended
columns.definition: A flag used for Observation Items only which indicates if the background color bar is to extend across the entire flowsheet for the item. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsInitiallyCollapsed
columns.definition: A flag used for Header, Observation Sets, and Observation Items which indicates if the item is initially contracted when the flowsheet is opened. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsBold
columns.definition: A flag that indicates if the display name should be in bold font. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsItalic
columns.definition: A flag that indicates if the display name should be in italic font. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsMandatory
columns.definition: A flag used for Observation Items and Observation Modifiers which indicates if the item is mandatory during data entry. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsInitiallyGraphed
columns.definition: A flag (used for Observation Items) only which indicates if the observation value is to be part of the default graph when viewing this flowsheet in the Trend View. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: GraphLevelNum
columns.definition: Integer field (used for Observation Items) only which contains the graph that this observation value should be displayed on.

columns.name: DefaultValueType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 1 = [None],2 = [Previous],3 = [Specific],

columns.name: SpecificDefault
columns.definition: Contains a specific value to default for the observation item or modifier when the flowsheet is displayed for data entry.

columns.name: IsPredefinedModifier
columns.definition: A flag used for Observation Modification items that indicates if it is a pre-defined modifier. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsDefaultProtected
columns.definition: A flag (used for Observation Modifiers only) which indicates if the default is protected, meaning that the user cannot change it during data entry. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: IsHidden
columns.definition: A flag used for Observation Modifiers which indicates if the modifier is to be displayed on this version of the flowsheet. 1 = True; 0 = False

columns.name: MSrepl_tran_version
columns.definition: Optimistic lock identifier.

columns.name: ShowAbnormalIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for an abnormal reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ShowVeryAbnormalIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for a very abnormal reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ShowHighIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for a High reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ShowVeryHighIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for a very high reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ShowLowIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for a low reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ShowVeryLowIcon
columns.definition: Specifies whether to display an icon for a very low reading or not. 1-display, 0-don't display

columns.name: ActivatedWhen

columns.name: CopyForwardHours
columns.definition: Specifies how many hours it can go back to 'copy forward' the data.

columns.name: DiscontinuedColor
columns.definition: Specifies the color to display for discontinued observations

columns.name: HeaderIndentation
columns.definition: Specifies the indentation of the header on the Structured Note

columns.name: FieldIndentation
columns.definition: Specifies the indentation of the field on the Structured Note

columns.name: FontColor
columns.definition: Color of the font selected

columns.name: FontFace
columns.definition: Specifies the font face

columns.name: Formula
columns.definition: Specifies the formula for the observation

columns.name: FutureDateTime
columns.definition: Enterprise TimeZone - The date and time in the future from when this row will be visible on the flowsheet and available for charting

columns.name: HighlightColor
columns.definition: Color to be displayed when an item is highlighted.

columns.name: IsFanOut
columns.definition: 1 indicates observations charted, will fan-out to other flowsheets. For 0 fan out will be turn off.

columns.name: IsRelatedData
columns.definition: 1 indicates related data will be visible for particular observation.

columns.name: IsRemovable
columns.definition: Stores 1 or 0 if the observation is removable or not

columns.name: ModifyComposition
columns.definition: Specifies whether composition can be modified for the parameter or not. 1-Modify allowed, 0-Cannot modify.

columns.name: RelativeTime
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [Start Of This Chart],1 = [Today],2 = [Yesterday],3 = [Three Days Ago],4 = [One Week Ago],5 = [Two Weeks Ago],6 = [One Month Ago],7 = [Three Months Ago],8 = [Six Months Ago],9 = [One Year Ago],

columns.name: ShadowColor
columns.definition: The shaded color

columns.name: MandateAbove
columns.definition: Specific Value the observations must be greater or equal to

columns.name: MandateBelow
columns.definition: Specific Value the observation must be less than or equal to

columns.name: MandateEqualValidValueGUID
columns.definition: The ValidValue that the current cell must be equal to

columns.name: MandateDepObsEntryItemGUID
columns.definition: The ObservationEntryItem that determines if the absolute Mandates are to be applied

columns.name: MandateGUID
columns.definition: The ObservationEntryItem that dictates the relative Mandate comparison Observation

columns.name: MandateType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [LessThan],1 = [GreaterThan],

columns.name: IsUnderLine
columns.definition: Indicates if item is underlined

columns.name: IsSignificant
columns.definition: Specifies whether the observation IsSignificant but not mandatory.

columns.name: SuppressCopyForward
columns.definition: Suppresses an observation for structured notes not to copy forward the observation into the next note

columns.name: DefaultPreviousDocGUID
columns.definition: Points to the actual place where the defaults come

columns.name: DefaultPreviousOEIGUID
columns.definition: Points to the actual parameter where the defaults come

columns.name: DefaultPreviousSourceType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [Any Document],1 = [This Document],2 = [Specific Document],

columns.name: IsReferenceItemInNote
columns.definition: Whether to reference the prior source in the note

columns.name: CopyForwardUnitType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [Hours],1 = [Days],2 = [Weeks],3 = [Months],

columns.name: OnChangeMLM
columns.definition: The name of the MLM that will be executed when this item is charted or changed

columns.name: DefaultVisitScopeType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [This Visit],1 = [This Chart],2 = [All Available],

columns.name: ApplyDocEntryType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [None],1 = [Specific Value],2 = [Previous Value],

columns.name: ApplyDocEditType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 0 = [None],1 = [Specific Value],2 = [Previous Value],

columns.name: IsEOV
columns.definition: Indicates whether the pull set will participate in EOV (End of Visit) calculations. This is enabled only when the pull set = Health Issues or Outpatient Medication Profile or Orders. When enabled, the record participates in the EOV (End of Visit) calculation as if it were in the pre 5.0 Assessment and Plan Section

columns.name: SuppressSaveInNote
columns.definition: Should the charting of this item be suppressed when the note is saved?

columns.name: AutoEnterMLMName
columns.definition: The new field stores the name of the MLM that will be invoked if auto enter is selected for that observation on the flowsheet. It can be configured for each observation on a flowsheet in the FlowSheet Catalog.

columns.name: IsSuppressExternalObsIn
columns.definition: Turns on/off allowing inbound obs from external system for each parameter

columns.name: IsSuppressExternalObsOut
columns.definition: Turns on/off allowing outbound obs from external system for each parameter

columns.name: IsUsePatientCharSelected
columns.definition: Used to determine whether observation is configured to use patient characteristics value for auto enter.

columns.name: IsFanIn
columns.definition: If this column is true then Fan-In is allowed and if false then fan-in is not allowed (suppressed). This will be set for the flowsheet versions.

columns.definition: Guid linked to the Selected flowsheet version Item

columns.definition: Holds the bit value whether to hide the Smart Pump alert window or not at the observation level.

tables.definition: This table will contain the columns available to the user to select for displaying in the Location Searching. This table is being created to satisfy business requirements in specification 30-4026 Changes to Location Search. Previously, the columns displayed in a Location Search grid were system defined and unalterable, but now the users will be able to define which columns they would like to see in the grid. There can only be one definition per facility, and it is either active or inactive. If inactive, the default columns will be displayed. columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 1 = [User],

columns.name: Level1Column
columns.definition: Store the first level column value of the preference that this favorite will be for. For Example: This preference is for section/set. Level1Column will store "PatCareDocGUID" value.

columns.name: Level1ColumnType
columns.definition: Store the type of level 1 column. For Example: Level1Column was PatCareDocGUID so store the name of the column here. (PatCareDocGUID = 1)

columns.name: Level2Column
columns.definition: Store the second level column value of the preference that this favorite will be for. For Example: This preference is for section/set Level2Column will store "ObsEntryItemGUID" value.

columns.name: Level2ColumnType
columns.definition: Store the type of level 2 column. For Example: Level 2 Column was ObsEntryItemGUID so store the name of the column here. (ObsEntryItemGUID = 1)

columns.name: FavoriteValue
columns.definition: store the preference item value. For Example: the 'FontColor' the user chooses is 'Red', or 'True' he wants to 'Hide' a tile, or 'True' to enable 'Scroll Bars.' Store 'Red', 'True', or 'True'

columns.name: FavoriteType
columns.definition: An enumerated type with the following list of possible values: 1 = [Default],2 = [ScrollBar],

tables.definition: The Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail tables are where the Pharmacy system writes data that will trigger the creation of a Financial Transaction segment.An external process will poll these tables and look for new transactions to send to the Financial System (Charge Control = 'NP').When the external process has sent the data to to the Financial System, it sets the status to processed (Charge Control = 'PD').The data in these tables is formatted in HL7 format.A Financial Transaction is made up of 1 row in Bill Charge Header, and 1 or more rows in Bill Charge Detail.The Bill Charge Header row contains the information that will go in the PID segment of the Financial Transaction.Each Bill Charge Detail row contains the information that will go in the FT1 segments of the Financial Transaction.After storing the data for the new Financial Transaction into these tables, Pharmacy's job is done and as far as Pharmacy is concerned, it has no more work to do. It is the responsibility of the external process to make sure that the transactions are sent to the Financial System.

columns.definition: Auto generated unique primary key value.

columns.definition: A foreign key to the EventSeriesDefinitionID column in the SXAHMEventSeriesDefinition table.

columns.name: PrevSequenceNumber
columns.definition: Defines the sequential number of previous occurrence, for which this rule is defining the spacing, relative to the current sequence number. For example, if the SequenceNumber is 3, and the PrevSequenceNumber is 1, then we are defining the spacing relationship that occurrence 3 has with occurrence 1.

columns.name: SequenceNumber
columns.definition: Defines the sequential number of occurrence that this rule is for. For example, if the SequenceNumber is 3, then we are defining the gap rules between occurrence 3 and the occurrence indicated by the PrevSequenceNumber column.

columns.name: CurrentAgeMin
columns.definition: The minimum client age at which this rule applies. An alphanumeric string representing an age. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: CurrentAgeMax
columns.definition: The maximum client age at which this rule applies. An alphanumeric string representing an age. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: PrevOccurrenceAgeMin
columns.definition: This rule only applies if the previous occurrence was completed after this minimum client age. An alphanumeric string representing an age. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: PrevOccurrenceAgeMax
columns.definition: This rule only applies if the previous occurrence was completed before this maximum client age. An alphanumeric string representing an age. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: GapMin
columns.definition: The minimum amount of time that is allowed to elapse between the scheduling completion of the occurrence represented by the SequenceNumber column, and the completion of the occurrence represented by the PrevSequenceNumber column.An alphanumeric string representing an amount of time. Accepted values will be all of, or part of, this format: ##y##m##w###d

columns.name: IsFinalOccurrence
columns.definition: Flag to indicate that this occurrence, as indicated by the SequenceNumber column, becomes the last occurrence of the series because it is completed so late that any further occurrences can no longer be scheduled or completed. For example, if occurrence 3 is given too late, then occurrence 3 completes the series and occurrence 4 can no longer be scheduled.

tables.definition: This entity contains a list of Price Algorithms that are defined for the entire enterprise. A Price Algorithm defines how the Cost (determined by the Charge Algorithm) is used to calculate the Price (amount to bill). A Price Algorithm can be Active or Inactive, and can include markups, fees, a rounding option, and minimum price functionality. In addition, the Price Algorithm can be tiered, so a different set of rules can be applied based upon which range (Cost From / Cost To) the Cost falls into. Each Price Algorithm can be associated with multiple Generic Items.

tables.definition: This table will maintain the relationship between Facilities and the Location Search columns defined for them. This table is being created to satisfy business requirements in specification 30-4026 Changes to Location Search. Previously, the columns displayed in a Location Search grid were system defined and unalterable, but now the users will be able to define which columns they would like to see in the grid. There can only be one definition per facility, and it is either active or inactive. If inactive, the default columns will be displayed. This table maintains the relationship between a facility and the selected columns

tables.definition: The Billed Transaction and Billed Transaction Detail tables contain the Audit History for the Billing Interface. This data represents the parameters used to generate the data in the Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail tables below. Financial Transaction Billed Audit Trail Financial Transaction consists of one Billed Transaction and 1 or more Billed Transaction Details. There is one Billed Transaction for each Bill Charge Header There is one Billed Transaction Detail for each Bill Charge Detail. If there was an Error returned by Determine Price, the Billing Interface will still create a Billed Transaction and the associated Billed Transaction Detail records, but will not create corresponding Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail rows. Billed Transaction Billed Transaction identifies Patient and Order related information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the PID segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System. Billed Transaction Detail Billed Transaction Detail identifies Drug, Cost, and Price information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the FT1 segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System. Billed Transaction Billed Transaction identifies Patient and Order related information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the PID segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System. Billed Transaction Detail Billed Transaction Detail identifies Drug, Cost, and Price information used to generate a Financial Transaction. This information is maintained for audit purposes, and used to derive the data that populates the FT1 segment in the Financial Transaction sent to the Financial System.

tables.definition: We need a way to save and retrieve information when a user �copy forwards by reference� information from a previous note. This could be a Section or Set (or potentially any Observation Entry item). Example: In the current Structured Notes, if someone has values from an earlier note that they wish to �copy forward into the current note�, then they selected the sections, and the data is saved, giving the impression that everything copy forwarded was performed at the date/time of the current note. In 4.0, we need to provide a �reference� to an older document, so, you can �copy forward by reference� (instead of by value!) the responses from the earlier note, and it would be displayed on the note �Referenced from (5/13/2003)� (or whatever date). This way, someone reading the note will know that a QA / PW / Observation / History section was done at an earlier date.

tables.definition: The Bill Charge Header and Bill Charge Detail tables are where the Pharmacy system writes data that will trigger the creation of a Financial Transaction segment. An external process will poll these tables and look for new transactions to send to the Financial System (Charge Control = 'NP'). When the external process has sent the data to to the Financial System, it sets the status to processed (Charge Control = 'PD') The data in these tables is formatted in HL7 format. A Financial Transaction is made up of 1 row in Bill Charge Header, and 1 or more rows in Bill Charge Detail. The Bill Charge Header row contains the information that will go in the PID segment of the Financial Transaction. Each Bill Charge Detail row contains the information that will go in the FT1 segments of the Financial Transaction. After storing the data for the new Financial Transaction into these tables, Pharmacy's job is done and as far as Pharmacy is concerned, it has no more work to do. It is the responsibility of the external process to make sure that the transactions are sent to the Financial System.

columns.definition: Identifies the Charge Code from the Charge Algorithm. The code assigned by the institution for the purpose of uniquely identifying the transaction.Components: ^ ^ ^ ^ ^ Component Values:1. SXAMMChargeAlgorithm.ChargeCode (Returned by Determine Price)2. The Generic Item Name for the Stock Item Product being billed (Returned by Determine Price)3. �SMM�4. SXAMMProduct.AlternateBillingCode5. Null6. �FIM�Components 4, 5, and 6 are only sent if the Alternate Billing Code (SXAMMProduct.AlternateBillingCode) exists.

columns.name: TransactionDesc

columns.name: TransactionQty
columns.definition: Identifies the quantity (number of units) billed, based on the Billing Preference UOM for the Generic Item.If there is no Billing Preference UOM for this Generic Item, then the UOM for the Cost record is used.Transaction Amount Ext = Transaction Amount * Transaction Quantity

columns.name: TransactionExtAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Price calculated for the Stock Item Product,Transaction Amount Ext = Transaction Amount * Transaction Quantity

columns.name: TransactionUnitAmt
columns.definition: Identifies the Unit Price based on the Billing Preference UOM for the Generic Item. If there is no Billing Preference UOM for this Generic Item, then this is the Unit Price based on the UOM for the Cost record.,Transaction Amount Ext = Transaction Amount * Transaction Quantity

columns.name: OrderedByCode

columns.name: FillerOrderNumber
columns.definition: This order number used by SMM to uniquely identify the order.Components: ^ The components values are:1. Entity identifier is set to the Pharmacy Order Number (CV3Order.OrderNumber)2. Namespace ID is set to the Literal 'SMM'

columns.name: ProcedureCode
columns.definition: Identifies HCPCS J Code related billing information such as the J Code Identifier, and J Code Quantity assigned to the Charge.Components: ^ ^ ^ ^ ^ Components1. Identifier is set to the Charge Code.2. Description is set to the Generic Item Name.3. Name of Coding System is set to the literal 'JCODE'.4. Alternate Identifier is set to the number of J Code Units (Billable Units).5. Alternate Description is set to the literal 'UNITS',6. Name of Alternate Coding System is set to the literal 'QTY'

columns.name: CareProviderTypeCode
columns.definition: Care provider TypeCode. Defines which provider type that can release to patient. Link to TypeCode column in CV3CareProvider table. If UseDelegateRole is true, then this controls the provider type that can act as a delegate. If this column is null, and UseDelegateRole is true, then any provider type can act as a delegate. Finally, if this column is null and UseDelegateRole is false and CareProviderRoleTypeGUID is null, then any provider role type can release the result.

columns.name: CareProviderRoleTypeGUID
columns.definition: GUID of care provider role type. Defines which provider role can make results available. Link to GUID column of CV3CareProviderRoleType table. This column will be null if: UseDelegateRole is true or UseDelegateRole is false and CareProviderRoleType is null. In this case any Care Provider role can release the result.

tables.definition: IVPB and LVP order need to have specific information on the labels about the current bag number and the administration times. Orders are allowed to be modified that require the information for the currently dispensed bags to be reprinted. In order to properly re-print the label information with the new order parameters the original parameters need to be stored for comparison. Also because labels are printed for the current filling period and the next filling period by different processes we need to store the different IVPB and LVP parameter state for both processes. This table will contain data all filling period changes as an order is processed from start to stop.

tables.definition: A requirement for SHM is to have the ability to set a message priority, much like setting high priority in Outlook. The initial priority values are High, Medium, Low with the ability to have the customer customize these values via the bulk load process or by a future administration tool within SHM. To create other priorities, choose an appropriate PriorityCode and give it an ImportanceLevel relative to the others in the table. For example, to make a Medium-High Priority code choose an ImportanceLevel between the values of High and Medium (ie 13), to make an Ultra-High Priority, choose an ImportanceLevel of 100. If you need to create another priority in-between 2 other priorities and there is no �room� to fit an ImportanceLevel between these two values, you can multiply all ImportanceLevel values in this table by some factor (ie 5) to get more available ImportanceLevels to choose from.

tables.definition: Information which is applicable at the order set level. This table allows the order set to link back to its catalog order set and multi order form version used to enter the order set. This will facilitate the reorder from order set and display order set details functions. Rows are put into this table with the order set is entered.The table is also used to track which sub-sets are in the set. For example, if an order set contains two sub-sets, then three rows are put into this table when the set is ordered. Information in this table will control how orders within the set are grouped together for the purposes of maintenance. For example, it can control if an order must be released with other orders in the parent set or with other orders in the sub-set.Finally, CDS can now perform duplicate checking at the set level, which requires that we know when a set was started / stopped.
